696_setting_tooltips.text: Expected cell diameter in pixels. Cellpose 4 rescales the image by 30/diameter before segmentation, aligning the expected object size with the scale used to train CPSAM. Leave it None (blank) to use the magnification default, 2*magnification+80 px (120 px at 20x, 160 px at 40x). 0 and 'auto' are the same value, stored as 'auto': Cellpose estimates the size itself (a Cellpose 3 size model estimates it; Cellpose-SAM, which has no size model, segments at native scale). spacr.diameter.estimate_diameters estimates a value from the selected fields. Default None.

Objective magnification, used only to derive expected object sizes: pixel diameter is 2*mag+80 for cells, 0.75*mag+45 for nuclei and mag for pathogens, with min/max area limits of diameter^2/4 and diameter^2*10. A blank cell_diameter, nucleus_diameter or pathogen_diameter is segmented at that default diameter with every model, Cellpose-SAM included; an explicit number or 'auto' overrides it. Set this to the acquisition objective magnification (10, 20, 40 or 60). Default 40.

Expected nucleus diameter in pixels, used by Cellpose 4 to rescale the image by 30/diameter before segmentation. None (blank) uses the magnification default, 0.75*magnification+45 px (60 px at 20x, 75 px at 40x). 0 and 'auto' are the same value, stored as 'auto': Cellpose estimates the size itself (Cellpose-SAM segments at native scale). spacr.diameter.estimate_diameters estimates a value. Default None.

Expected pathogen diameter in pixels, used by Cellpose 4 to rescale the image by 30/diameter before segmenting. None (blank) uses the magnification default, magnification px (20 px at 20x, 40 px at 40x). 0 and 'auto' are the same value, stored as 'auto': Cellpose estimates the size itself (Cellpose-SAM segments at native scale). Intracellular parasites are often only a few pixels across at low magnification, where rescaling matters most. spacr.diameter.estimate_diameters proposes a value. Default None.

Multiples of the object diameter the robustness report tries, one at a time; a blank diameter counts as its magnification default and 0 or 'auto' as Cellpose's nominal 30 pixels. Default [0.75, 1.25].

696_UI.text: Pixels. Blank uses the magnification default (shown greyed); 0 or auto lets Cellpose estimate the diameter.
{value} is not a diameter: type a number of pixels, 0 or auto to let Cellpose estimate it, or clear the cell for the magnification default.

696_shared_diameter_tooltip.text: (float, px) Expected object diameter. Cellpose-SAM uses it: the image is rescaled by 30/diameter before segmentation, so raising it finds bigger objects and lowering it finds smaller ones. 30 is the no-op (30/30 = 1). 0 and auto are the same value: Cellpose estimates the size (Cellpose-SAM, which has no size model, keeps the native scale). An object diameter left blank opens at its magnification default, as the run uses it.

696_public_API.text:
Configuration for image preparation and Cellpose segmentation.

Parameters
----------
src:
    Plate folder, or a sequence of plate folders, containing the source
    microscopy images.
cell_channel, nucleus_channel, pathogen_channel:
    Zero-based intensity channel used for each segmentation target. Leave
    an object at ``None`` when it should not be segmented. At least one is
    required.
cell_diameter, nucleus_diameter, pathogen_diameter:
    Expected object diameters in pixels. ``None`` uses the
    magnification default (``2*magnification+80`` for cells,
    ``0.75*magnification+45`` for nuclei, ``magnification`` for
    pathogens); ``0`` or ``"auto"`` lets Cellpose estimate it.
channels:
    Intensity channels retained in the merged field arrays.
magnification:
    Objective magnification recorded with the run.
pipeline_style:
    ``"v1"`` for the stable disk-based pipeline or ``"v2"`` for the
    experimental streaming path.
extra:
    Advanced settings not represented by typed fields. Keys that repeat a
    typed field are refused so one script cannot contain two answers.
test_mode:
    Run Mask on a random subset of up to ``test_images`` complete image
    sets under ``<src>/test`` and enable diagnostic plots before
    processing the full source.
dry_run:
    Run Mask preflight and return its reported problems before heavy
    pipeline imports, model loading, segmentation, or writes.

Examples
--------
>>> config = MaskConfig(
...     "/data/plate01", cell_channel=0, nucleus_channel=1,
...     cell_diameter=60, nucleus_diameter=20,
... )
>>> settings = config.to_settings()
>>> settings["src"]
'/data/plate01'

Build the settings dict that the pipeline receives.

Layered lowest-to-highest: the module's own defaults, the settings file,
then the ``--set`` overrides. The file is read under today's names first
-- see :func:`_under_todays_names`, without which a value the file set
under an old name lost to the default already sitting under the new one.
An object diameter of 0 or "auto" comes out as "auto", the one form
both are stored in (item 696).

:param module: module being run.
:param settings_path: path to the settings file, or None for defaults only.
:param overrides: ``key=value`` strings.
:param moved: list to receive the migration notices, passed straight to
    :func:`_under_todays_names`; a caller that prints a pre-flight report
    hands these to :func:`_preflight` so the keys the fold consumed are
    still named there.
:returns: the fully-resolved settings dict.
:raises SettingsError: on any unreadable file, unknown key or bad value.

Make the form's own fields write into the table.

This is the form-to-grid half of the two-way binding. Without it, a
value changed outside the grid -- the flat row for an object the
table does not claim, a preset, the Live Preview, a loaded settings
file -- would leave the table showing the old value.

The table is not reseeded: `seed` rebuilds the whole table, which
takes 30 ms on Mask and 100 ms with ten organelles. On a
`textChanged` that would run per keystroke and move the cursor out
of the cell being edited. One cell is written instead.

The magnification field is followed as well: a blank object
diameter shows the magnification default, which moves with it
(item 696).

:returns: how many widgets were newly connected.

A single pipeline invocation's on-disk record.

Instances are produced by :func:`open_run`. Users don't construct
them directly.

:ivar app_key: id of the pipeline app that opened the run.
:ivar settings: settings dict originally passed to the pipeline.
:ivar dir: run folder path (``~/.spacr/runs/<ts>_<uuid>__<app>``).
:ivar start_ts: unix epoch seconds when the run opened.
:ivar end_ts: unix epoch seconds when the run closed (set by
    :func:`open_run` on exit).
:ivar status: ``"running"`` / ``"success"`` / ``"failed"`` /
    ``"cancelled"``. The last is a run the user stopped, which is not a
    run that broke, and the two want different things done next.
:ivar model_hashes: dict of ``{human-name: "filename:sha256-16"}``.
    Populated by callers via :meth:`record_model`.
:ivar model_files: full SHA-256, size, and path records for models.
:ivar input_hashes: per-file full SHA-256 input provenance.
:ivar output_hashes: per-file full SHA-256 output provenance.
:ivar seeds: declared seeds and runtime RNG-state identifiers.
:ivar provenance_warnings: non-fatal path/hash failures retained in the
    manifest instead of being silently discarded.
:ivar run_warnings: distinct warning lines emitted by the pipeline.
:ivar environment: host, spaCR, Git, and installed-package versions.
:ivar stages: consolidated FlowView lifecycle records in execution order.
:ivar stdout_path: captured standard-output log path, when one is attached.
:ivar error_traceback: formatted exception traceback for failed or
    cancelled runs; empty for successful runs.
:ivar diameters: per object, the diameter it was segmented with, e.g.
    ``"120 px (magnification 20x default)"`` or ``"auto (Cellpose
    estimated 57.3 px)"`` (item 696).
